uncited: - Input: The fixed-sized bucket data structure (min-dictionary, cell records, and optional marker cells), the previous isovalue $q$, the new isovalue $q'$, and the previous set of active buckets/cells.
- **Cell Records:** $N$ records, one for each cell in the dataset.
- **Min-Dictionary:** $N/B + 1$ values, storing the minimum intensity value for each bucket.
- **Marker Cells:** $N/B + 1$ additional cells (one per bucket) used to track the boundary between active and inactive cells within a bucket.
Empirical results show average active cell lookup time decreases toward 4096 and increases past 8192.
The algorithm distinguishes between increasing isovalue ($q' > q$) and decreasing isovalue ($q' < q$).
Let $c^*_0, \dots, c^*_a$ be the set of active buckets for the previous isovalue $q$, and $c^*_0, \dots, c^*_{a'}$ be the set for the new isovalue $q'$.
- These buckets were active in the previous query and remain active.
- Markers are pushed upward (t higher indices) to deactivate cells that are no longer active.
- This bucket now has a single contiguous block of active cells and a single contiguous block of inactive cells.
- These buckets were inactive in the previous query but are now active.
- These buckets were active in the previous query and remain active.
- Markers are pushed downward (to lower indices) to activate cells that are newly active.
- This bucket contains non-contiguous blocks of cells that must be activated and deactivated.
- These buckets were active in the previous query but are now inactive.
- **Pathological Worst-Case:** If only one cell is active and located at the bottom of the last bucket, the algorithm traverses $N/B$ buckets and $B$ inactive cells.
- **Average-Case:** $O(K + B)$, where $K$ is the number of active cells and $B$ is the bucket size.

This is derived from at most three comparisons per cell in a normal bucket (one max-criterion per active cell, one min-dictionary check, one failed max-criterion check per bucket) and at most two comparisons per cell in the last active bucket (bounded by $B$).
- **When to Use:** When isovalue changes are small and coherent, incremental extraction provides significant speedups.
